Import troubles : "If you have troubles importing your audio : \nZIP : In filepicker, if a click on a zip shows the content of the zip instead of letting you select the zip , try a long click on the zip. \nZIP : If Unzip fails, try tp unzip them before with another app. \nIf problem with picking audios from Download folder, try to move them out of 'Download' folder."

Memory Cleaning : A specific view to check the content of the Bookplayer internal memory does now exist. \n \nIt allows you to see which books do take a lot of room. You can delete some of them from here. \n \nPlease note that will show there, only books that have been copied inside Bookplayer internal reserved memory. \nThat is to say, all audios from ZIP file, + all audios from Single File / Folder, that have been loaded with the [copy] setting on (in menu/options)
Permissions : "BookPlayer can run without any permission. \nThere is 3 main permissions : \n[Music and Audio] = [Read Audio] = [External Storage] : Allows to read audio from the general device memory, if copy option was unselected (like from the download folder, the music folder, or any other one) \n\n[Microphone] (= [Record Audio]) is needed to display a frequency visualizer animation (sound spectrum display). If it is denied, it will just not show, no problem. \n\n[Notifications] may be needed on some devices (Android 14+). It is used to display the command widget on the lock screen. (Usually it displays straight away without permission being even asked.)"
Forum : I\'ve just set up a forum for users to discuss this app. (June 2025). \nAnyone can read posts, but you\'ll need to register your email to participate. \nFeel free to suggest improvements, share ideas, or report bugs. \nYou can also exchange tips—like where to find quality audiobooks and more.

File Types : Bookplayer can read many type of audios, even videos. Just try to load them! Best choice will always be [mp3] files, as a zip or in a folder. But Bookplayer can now read the new [m4b] file type. It will try to detect the chapters inside if any. If you use the new export capability, from a previously loaded m4b file, you will get a zip with chapters as aac audio files.
This activity starts with you picking a file or a folder. \nThen, 2 main possibilities : \n \noption 1 [copy] :default Bookplayer will first, copy the audio inside Bookplayer internal app memory, and then read it from there. \n \noption 2 [no copy] : Bookplayer will just register the location so as to directly play audio from the general device memory (E.g. from the Download folder, the Music folder or any folder) \n \n(Note that ZIP files are always copied, Split M4B as well. This option is only for direct read of simple audio files) \n \nWith option 1 (copy), you won\'t need the [Read Audio] permission. \nAlso, if you delete the file from main memory, or move it, that won\'t matter. You will not loose your book and progress. \n \nWith option 2 (no copy), you may save space. \n \nThere is another setting, in menu/options, that allows you to automatically delete the source file, once it has been imported. \nActivate that one if all the books you load into Bookplayer will not be needed by another app.
